title: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

sense.text:
“And by thy sword shalt thou live.” Esau was prophesied to live by the sword, and the military might the whole world is watching now is that prophecy. America is showing its strength overseas with its Air Force, its ground troops and its navy, and all those different levels of military action were prophesied in the Bible for one specific group of people.

That is why their leader can stand up and say, We are the strongest nation in the world, we have the strongest military by far, we don't need them. Esau said, We built this thing up. Satan gave them their powers. They only want to see who will chip in, who is loyal to the beast, and whether they still have power over the nations like they are supposed to.

For the last thirty or forty years our people could not see it because they were blinded. Barack Obama dropped a bomb every day of his term and nobody knew. Now, with smartphones and social media, you see eight different countries bombed in a span of a few months, and you see America for who they truly are: warmongers. Esau is not the Arabs. The Bible says this man would live by the sword.

“And I saw, and behold a white horse”: the white horse is the Edomite nations. “He that sat on him had a bow; and a crown was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer.”

What did they call the European settlers? Conquistadors. All of them came from Europe, and all of them come from Esau. That is the nation we are seeing today. The beast is not the Arabs and it is not the Roman Catholic Church. It is Esau, led primarily by America.

We have to know our enemy in these last days, because Christianity and religion have deceived us for far too long. People are asking why this nation is bombing innocent women and children and calling the other side evil. These are the times when the wicked shall be revealed.

“Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts.” All of us should desire certain things in the spirit: when you see a brother's charitable spirit, his spirit in building, in editing, in dealing with the public, in ordering events, you should desire those spiritual gifts.

“But rather that ye may prophesy.” That is why prophecy has to be dealt with before anything else. The Christian church is not dealing with anything going on in the earth; it is still trying to collect tithes and run your W-2, telling you color doesn't matter. Meanwhile this man is being revealed to the whole world, and every news update can be channeled straight to the scriptures.

The purpose of prophecy is to build your spirit up and prepare you for temptation and destruction. Prophecy is a warning, thus saith the Lord: when you see these things come to pass, know that Esau, Edom, America, is the enemy the Bible speaks of.

“And the fourth kingdom shall be strong as iron: forasmuch as iron breaketh in pieces and subdueth all things.” The iron is the military might of this last kingdom. Their own leader said it: three of the top five air forces in the world are theirs, the number one navy is theirs; they are so much more powerful than anybody else. That is the iron.

“The kingdom shall be divided; but there shall be in it of the strength of the iron, forasmuch as thou sawest the iron mixed with miry clay.” The clay is all the nations trying to join together inside it. The same leader said that on the back end you have psychological warfare, racism, men against women, the races turned against each other. What he described is straight out of the scriptures.

“So the kingdom shall be partly strong, and partly broken.” This kingdom is America. It can go anywhere and do anything it wants: it went into Venezuela, cut off the lights, grabbed Maduro and left; it bombed Nigeria overnight; it held a peace meeting with Iran and bombed them at the same time. And nothing has happened at home. We are still doing TikTok dances, going to the movies, worrying about the NFL draft. That is the strong part.

But before this war broke out, Minnesota was talking civil war over ICE. Everybody was saying there was going to be a civil war, and America said, No, we are going to war with somebody else. That is how this nation is partly strong and partly broken.

“They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men”: that is interracial marriage and the interracial mingling. All nations were never supposed to be together the way they are here. In Deuteronomy he gave this nation this land and that nation that land; the white man said, No, we want everybody together.

“But they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay.” Iran has no problem uniting its citizens. Iraq has no problem. Great Britain has no problem. No other nation has this problem except this one, because it has all nations here, and all religions here too. How is a Muslim going to connect with a Christian, or a Christian with an atheist? Atheism is a religion too; they believe people came out of frogs. One of the reasons they bombed Iran is that it does not have their kind of freedoms, the freedom to identify as a dog. That is why this kingdom is partly divided, and it gives you clues all day long who this last beast is.
“And the ten horns which thou sawest are ten kings”: the ten horns are NATO. They “receive power as kings one hour with the beast”, and they have been in bed with America since 1945.

“These have one mind”: they have been in agreement this whole time, letting America do whatever it wants while nobody says anything. “And shall give their power and strength unto the beast.” The news said it plainly: since 1945 they have relied on the strength of the American military to defend themselves. That is how they give their power unto the beast.

What did America do in World War II that no other nation ever did? It dropped atomic bombs on two cities. That is fire coming down from heaven. Nuclear deterrence, intelligence networks and strategic leadership have been the backbone of the whole alliance; the security of all these nations has been built around the United States. So the beast is not the Arabs and not the Roman Catholic Church. It is America, make no mistake about it.

“These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings.” They will make war with Christ, and Christ will overcome them, “and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful.”

“The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” From Revelation 17:1, the beast and the woman are the same people: this last kingdom, America. As Daniel 2 showed, this is where all people are located, and America is in every land among every people.

“And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore.” That is what was just seen with our own eyes: in the middle of the night, 3:47 in the morning in Brussels, representatives of 28 nations signed a new security alliance for Europe designed to function without the United States. America came out of Europe, out of the UK, but it is not of them. They were fine with him while he fought for them; now they see he is not rolling the way he is supposed to. All of this is happening before your eyes while the Christian church has you clapping on a tambourine and hiding the gay choir director.

They “shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” The fire she will be burned with is nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missiles. That is what is coming to America.

The Bishops and Deacons have been teaching this for years: NATO is going to fight against America. People asked how it could happen when they were locked tight and moving in unison. Now you see it, and the Christians are not even looking at Revelation; they say the book is sealed.

“For God hath put in their hearts to fulfil his will”: the Most High designed all of it. That is why you can sit back and watch the news without worrying; we know exactly what is going to happen before it happens. So how are they going to say God bless America? God is not blessing America. They will agree and give their kingdom unto the beast “until the words of God shall be fulfilled.”
“And the woman which thou sawest is that great city, which reigneth over the kings of the earth.” That great city is America.

precepts.why:
What is being read out of Revelation, all the prophets saw: they saw the same vision. “For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie.” That means it is guaranteed. Everything read in Isaiah, in Habakkuk and in Revelation shall not fail.

“Though it tarry, wait for it”: we hear the Bishop bring out the revelations and the breakdowns, and it is tarrying, taking its time, while the Christians are oblivious, distracted with money and the prosperity doctrine. Wait for it is the counsel given to the elect: be patient and get yourself right, because the vision will come to pass and the nations will turn on each other.

“Because it will surely come, it will not tarry.” How will it happen? Trump is the white Debo; he will say and do anything and take everybody's stuff. Just as the Most High hardened Pharaoh's heart, this man is so proud he clowned the leader of Japan to her face about Hiroshima and Pearl Harbor. That pride is how the ten horns will come to hate her.

How could the nations benefit so much from America and then grow to hate her? This is why. “Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon”: the virgin daughter of Babylon is America. People try to say Babylon is somewhere else, but when has America ever been touched? The one thing that ever happened, they did themselves: 9/11 was the biggest controlled demolition anybody has ever witnessed. So Babylon is not these other nations.

She is the one Revelation 17 speaks of, and she is the virgin. Virgin means nobody has touched her, destroyed her or defiled her, until these prophecies are fulfilled. “There is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.” She thought she was tender and delicate, but that is coming to an end; she will be touched. All manner of nations live inside her, as Daniel 2:43 shows, America's enemies and sleeper cells included.

“Uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh.” A virgin would be covered, but the wickedness of Babylon, America, is being revealed. “Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance.” Her shame is how she allies herself with little Satan and helps them bomb other countries, the demolition project to wipe out Gaza and all the people there, and renaming a whole body of water the Gulf of America. This man is the devil the Bible speaks of. And the word to our people is to come out of her: come out of religion, these doctrines and Christianity, the lies and philosophies, and repent.

sense.text:
When America struck Iran, it went after the leaders first: the Ayatollah, then the set of leaders under him, then the next set, until, in their own words, nobody wants to be a leader and there is nobody left to talk to. Cut off the head and the body shall fall. That is how the white man wages war, and it is a message for us that we had better take to heart.

“And the dragon was wroth with the woman”: the woman is Israel. He “went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.” This is how he goes to war: he attacks the leaders. A man who can bomb somebody on the other side of the earth in a second knows exactly where we are; we pay for his internet, we use his GPS, we pay taxes, we ask ChatGPT everything.

So all of us must have the mindset of a leader. You may be a 10 today and over the whole congregation tomorrow. That is why the Bishop is so hard on us about every city operating as its own headquarters, and every leader having a circle, a cabinet around him that he can trust. Look at Iran: the leader was killed and nothing stopped. Their intelligence was set up all over the country and everybody operates independently; they watched the mistakes of Iraq and planned for years. Every morning they still send missiles to Tel Aviv while Trump says everybody is dead. They have some captains somewhere they did not get. God forbid something should happen, the brothers cannot just stop the mission.

precepts.why:
If anybody knows that tactic of warfare, it should be us. Every leader who stood up for the nation of Israel, even without knowing he was an Israelite, was murdered: Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, Fred Hampton, Medgar Evers; Marcus Garvey was exiled; and in Africa the African leaders were all killed. Now it is shown again in this last week's time, so you do not have to guess.

“Who will rise up for me against the evildoers? or who will stand up for me against the workers of iniquity?” The Most High is looking for those who will stand up, and not when everything is great. You are not a leader when everything is in order. Who is going to stand up when the president who has reigned for 29 years is dead and the whole country is being bombed left and right? Who is going to set things in order then? That is where we are right now spiritually as a nation.

That tactic has been the same for Esau forever, and it happened to Christ. “When Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king”: Herod was an Edomite, Esau. The wise men came “Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews?” Christ is our leader, the King of the Jews.

Then reading on: “for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” Esau is always threatened when his people have a leader other than him. When Esau is not ruling over you, he feels some type of way and starts taking out your leaders, anyone who can gather the poor of God's people together.

“Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem.” He got mad that the wise men did not give up the King of the Jews, so he tried to kill Christ and killed every child two years old and under, everybody who could potentially be a leader, whoever could fill his spot. Just as he did in Iran: he killed everybody who could potentially be a leader. The spirit in this man has not changed, and blood will come to him.

sense.text:
Each and every one of us in the nation of Israel has the spirit in us to be a leader. If you are in this room or watching this class, God is calling you to lead. We are as the sand of the sea and only a third of our people will repent, so each one of us is a weapon for the Most High God. You could be at the soccer game, the doorbuster at JCPenney or the movies, but God called you here to get yourself together in this truth, and that alone sets you up to be a leader in the coming kingdom, not then but now. Leadership is taught; all you have to do is apply yourself.

“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee.” God chose each of us for the position we are in right now. If you have fringes on and understand the Sabbath, you are in the top .0001% of the earth, and you know what many people do not. You are a leader the second you walk into your job.

“To be a special people unto himself.” A special person does not just do what everybody else does; in sports the special one is usually the leader of the group just because he has a talent. Your talent is keeping God's commandments, wisdom and understanding nobody else has. “Above all people that are upon the face of the earth”: that does not sound like a people made to be followers. We follow Christ and we follow the leaders, not these nations.

precepts.why:
“And what one nation in the earth is like thy people, even like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself.” There is no nation of people like us. We were brought over here on slave ships, chained, unable to read or write, not knowing where we were, and somehow we figured it out and tried to get out of there; don't let the white man fool you, there were a whole bunch of slave rebellions. We knew this man was not better than us.

Today most of our people cannot survive without a cell phone, yet we are built different. The white man has every advantage in the world and still ends up a vagabond on the side of the street.

What makes us different is what God gave us. We have the cheat code; we tap into something nobody else gets to tap into, and that makes us wise, great leaders and great judges. “Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments”: we are held accountable on a level no other nation is, because he never judged any other nation the way he judged us.

“Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations.” Yet many throw the Bible away the second they are around people without fringes and lose all their wisdom. That wisdom is what separates you and puts you in a leadership position; they see the spirit on you. It is what elevated Daniel and Joseph to high levels of leadership in the heathen's kingdom, by applying what was taught to them.

“Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” All of us have the capacity to lead. Only a third of our people will repent, but those who are keeping the commandments were set up for a reason, not to sit and collect dust: lead in your household, your office, the 20 men under you, the sisters you teach, the city, the country, guided by the commandments of God and the faith of Christ.

“What nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law”? No other nation has what we have. All their leadership books, which make billions in leadership conferences, are based on the Bible: a chapter title, a scripture, then their writings. They get the watered-down version; we get the pure concentrate, because it was only given to us. So how is it they rule over us?

Many of our brothers and sisters have been destroyed and do not see themselves as a prince, a ruler or a judge, but God says you are all of those things. This is talking about the same Israelites as Deuteronomy 4. The church at Corinth was not white Grecians in togas, and the Galatians are not the white man in Turkmenistan. It is talking about you.

“But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people.” God says you are separate from everybody else. Nobody lights a candle and puts it under a bushel; it is time for your light to shine, and you do not shine from the back, you shine from the front. It is time for all of us to take our places.

What makes us peculiar? “Serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them.” That is what separates us: the fringes on your dress, the beard on your face, not going out with them on Saturday because you keep the Sabbath. They thought you were a Christian, and they do not even know the ten commandments.

Those commandments “were given unto them”: all these things were given only to us.

“He will magnify the law.” That is each and every one of our jobs: to put the laws of God on a pedestal and stand firm for them. When you do, it automatically puts you in a different position, different from everybody else on the face of the earth, because nobody else is standing firm for the commandments, and it sets you up to be a leader.

The way you do anything is the way you do everything. A brother asked how he could do better, and the answer was to try to be the leader on his job; none of the managers were better than him, but his mindset was not there. Most of the time the one over you is no better than you; you wonder how this cracker is over you, and it is because you are not doing things according to the commandments.

That separation shows. In Houston the women dressed so out of order at spring break that a regional dress code had to be put in place, while our sisters dress modestly, and the whole show stops when they show up. On a cruise where the other black men are trying to get drunk and get women, a group of 50 men reading the Bible becomes the disturbance. They make a man an offender for the word, but if something happened on that ship they would come asking the Bible-loving guys for help.

sense.text: “Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.” These were “men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring prophecies.”

“Leaders of the people”: not one leader, not two, leaders. We are a nation of leaders. That is why it says to the law and to the prophets: there were many prophets and many holy women throughout the scriptures who were leaders. That is the nation you come from. Their knowledge of learning was “meet for the people”, just right for what the people needed in that time, stage and area.

“Such as found out musical tunes”: brothers in music are leaders in music. We need leaders in every facet of life, because one man cannot build a nation by himself; the Bishop has told us for years this work is too big for one man. “And recited verses in writing”: that is why you see brothers and sisters making books, like Captain O'Shea. That is not out-and-out ordinary; that is what we did.

“Rich men furnished with ability, living peaceably in their habitations.” Brothers with ability, with leaders under them in every office. They were able to take their wisdom and calm the area they were in, living peaceably with their neighbors, like David, who had all nations in subjection, so that Solomon lived peaceably during his reign.

“All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times. There be of them, that have left a name behind them, that their praises might be reported.” Their leadership was so astounding that we read about it in the Bible and try to extract how they did it. The Bible is the number one selling book every year, and almost every great book quotes it; it is the greatest book with the greatest knowledge ever.

We must step into our vocation and not be afraid of being great. The Lord compares us to fine gold, and gold is not easy to get; you have to mine for it. A leader is needed to bring comfort to a people in decay, to those who have been robbed, raped and murdered, and no nation on this planet needs great leaders more than ours.

“Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which thou shalt wound the adversaries.” This is Judas Maccabeus preparing the men for war. We are at war, brothers, against sin and against our physical enemies, the children of Satan, Edom, Esau.

“Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas”: not Judas's own mindset, the words of God. The words of God comfort people who have a spirit of fear and stir them up to be courageous in the time of fear. That is why we have leaders, and that is why the nations destroy the leaders first: in some cases the leaders are the lifeline of the people.

His words were able “to stir them up to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men, they determined not to pitch camp, but courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict.” That is the result of a great leader: through comfort he stirred the people up to try the matter in battle, and gave them the wisdom they needed to fight against evil.

precepts.why:
How do you become a man known for giving comfort to the people like Judas? “And this was his vision”: leaders are visionaries, and where there is no vision the people perish.

“That Onias, who had been high priest, a virtuous and a good man”: the root of virtuous is virtue, moral excellence. Our moral compass is God's commandments, which make us shine like gold. He was “reverend in conversation, gentle in condition”: he kept his composure and was not hot-headed, and “well spoken also”.

“And exercised from a child in all points of virtue.” Leading is not a one-off thing where you wake up and lead people; we are born leaders, but we have to become that in time. “Holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews”: leaders serve and sacrifice themselves for the betterment of the people.

To be a leader you have to know the condition of the battle. If the first time you are hearing that there is a war going on is now, almost a month in, you are asleep.

“And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets”: if you are not comforting yourself, your children, your wife or your husband out of the law and the prophets, you are not leading. “Putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.” This puts you in mind that there is a war, a spiritual war. The bombs will drop because the Lord said so; but are you mentally prepared when famine comes and your children are looking at you?

“And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths.” We have to show that Esau is the devil, lying about this and that, breaking all kinds of treaties and oaths. If your daughter secretly wants to be Tinkerbell or wear the Frozen wig, she does not see the breach of oaths in Esau. As a mother or father you must rework her mind and put her in the mindset of our fathers.

sense.text:
Willie Lynch's method was to keep the slave physically strong but psychologically weak and dependent on the slave master: keep the body, take the mind. That is where the men are, and that is why the Bishop and the Deacons teach the way they teach. We are in a decayed estate. The mindset of 99% of our people is in a horrible state: women think they can wear tights outside, grown men go outside in a crop top with the belly out, young women are out on the dance teams. If that does not put you in a different state of mind, you are destroyed. That is why we teach loud in the streets.

“They said one to another”: nobody tried to do it by himself. When the Bishop went to the streets he had a reader; that is why the scriptures say go two by two. “Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people”: that is what you see in IUIC, our women in order, our men in order, our children in order.

“And let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” You will go much further and sacrifice much more for someone else than for yourself. Selfish people only go so far, because at some point they are satisfied.

“If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”: you are the interpreter, brother, and you are that one among a thousand. That makes you a leader, and you have to have the mind of a leader. Any place you step into, your mindset should not be to fit in but to figure out how to make it better. Joseph did not go into Egypt and just sit there; he asked how the problem was going to be solved. He did not just get by on a nine-to-five. The Lord gave us wisdom, discretion, judgment and skill sets.

Like Django said, I am that one in ten thousand: that is you, each and every one of you. When you show up on the job, you are not like the rest of them. That is the mindset of a leader, and the first part of it is that a leader believes he can get the job done. That is what separates you from everybody else.

When an issue arises, a leader does not run. He raises his hand, volunteers and figures out a solution. That is the first thing: the mind to get the job done, and the Lord has put that in your spirit.

“Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Who is going to go on our behalf? “Then said I, Here am I; send me.” That is the mindset of a leader. It is what David did: Where is Goliath? All of you keep crying about the situation; show me. The first thing you must have is a willingness and a belief in completing the task, whatever it may be, and that mindset alone sets you apart.

precepts.why:
The mindset of a leader sees a problem and believes he can solve it, because before you do anything you have to visualize it. You have to see it before you see it. Whether you graduated, got married or got a job, you visualized it in your mind before it happened.

“Though all the nations that are under the king's dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers”, he said, “Yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers.” Mattathias saw two realities: one where his children sacrificed to devils, ate swine and were like everybody else, and one where they fought and won. He had to have the mindset not to bow down to sin and the heathen. “We will not hearken to the king's words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.” Our religion is keeping the commandments; somebody who says he has no religion does not know what he is talking about.

When a Jew came to sacrifice on the altar at Modin, Mattathias “was inflamed with zeal”, slew him upon the altar, killed the king's commissioner and pulled down the altar, dealing “zealously for the law of God like as Phinees did unto Zambri the son of Salom.” Then he cried, “Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me.”

Somebody had to stand up with the mindset that we are not going to do what everybody else is doing. That is the decision the Bishops made years ago with no internet, no YouTube, no followers: we cannot do this Christian church again; come to the basement and we will figure something out. Each of you made the same decision: I don't know where the school is, but I am going to call this number, drive three hours, come every other week, tune into the class. You had to make that decision to be a leader, because it is easy to follow.

Remember that first confidence: we stopped wearing pants, stopped eating pork, stopped keeping Christmas, and our faith led us to safe havens in this truth. The wisdom given to us supersedes the wisdom of this earth; we understand the beginning and the end of time. Christ is King of kings and Lord of lords, the boss of all bosses, which means you are the bosses and must conduct yourself that way. Take your hand off the plow and you fall in with Jonah, who fled the work until the Lord raised the storm and put him in the mouth of a fish. Don't make excuses not to do the work given to you.

Passover season is coming, and the tree gets shaken every Passover. If you are on the fence about going back to the church or keeping Easter because your mama bought you a white dress and a tall hat, don't fall out of that tree.

sense.text: This is a characteristic of the leaders in IUIC, unlike every other so-called leader, Michael Jordan or a football coach. “Being assembled with one accord”: the Bishops on one accord, the Deacons on one accord, the Captains on one accord. “To send chosen men unto you”: not just anybody is sent out, chosen men, “with our beloved Barnabas and Paul”, as you would say Bishop Nathanyel or Deacon Isaac.

“Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.” A real leader risks his life for Christ. Michael Jordan is not risking anything; Wyclef is not. Captains and officers have been to Haiti, to Africa, to the barrios of Puerto Rico, and we are not going to the suburbs, we are going to the hood all over IUIC. This is not play play. Women must fall in line and respect their man; King David would not deal with the woman who disrespected him in the time of war.

Leaders build leaders. That is an attribute of a father: a father wants his son to be better than him. A leader's mission is to build future leaders better than himself, which is what the Bishops are doing, raising up leaders who reach corners that were never touched before. If your mindset is job security, sitting in the high places without building other brothers to be better than you, the Lord will remove you.

The next point: the leader believes he can get the job done and invites others with him, like Mattathias saying, Follow me. Christ did the same. He came to Capernaum “in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim”, “Galilee of the Gentiles”, which was Israelites. “The people which sat in darkness saw great light.”
“From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” Christ saw an issue: his people had to be taught the right way.

He did not try to do everything by himself. He saw “two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.” All he saw was two fishermen, but he saw something in them that he could use, and said, “Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” A great leader's job is to make other leaders. Not everybody will come in with everything together, married with two kids and a picket fence; it is our job to restore you to your rightful place as a man, as a god on this earth.

“And they straightway left their nets.” There are two parts: the leader has to invite you, and you have to accept it. Many fight the invitation. Every week we tell the brothers MOV is starting; the sisters are asked to help with security or in the kitchen, and they just sit there looking at the chair. They left their nets straightway: I get to work with Christ? I'm out.

You joined what people call the greatest movement on earth, and you sit and do nothing. A Lakers fan at least buys a jersey; a Yankees fan goes to the game. You catch every game on league pass and know everybody's stats for 13 years, but come into the truth and don't know what the light is.

precepts.why:
“He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” All the understanding and wisdom was given to us, not the other nations, so there is no reason to sit on it and do nothing.

“Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.” That is Christ. We are the only ones that have a God, and our God saw us so special that he, Emmanuel, walked with us and conversed with us. That is the same thing as Matthew 4 when he said, Follow me: our leader telling us to follow him.

Our God saw fit to walk with us, teach us and guide us, and we have to do the same in waking up our brothers and sisters. “The Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant”: you were made to be the servant of God and to do this work, not to be a basketball player or a rapper. “To bring Jacob again to him”: that is your commission.

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”: a light thing, the least you can do. Our God came down and sacrificed himself for you; doing the work of the Lord and waking up your people is a light thing.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” It is the same as Matthew 4: we go to our brothers, the northern kingdom in Galilee of the Gentiles, carrying on the mission God gave us.

sense.text: Once again, the leader believes he can get the job done. He does not have an unsure mindset; he says, Send me, follow me. “The Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia”, who proclaimed, “Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the Lord God of Israel.”

“Then rose up the chief of the fathers of Judah and Benjamin”: the leaders. They said, We can go back, we are out. The Bishop always speaks about this time period: our people were established in the countries where they were. Imagine Trump saying today, Who wants to go back to Jerusalem, we will give you the land. A whole bunch of Negroes would say no. The men who went back were not ordinary men; they saw a vision and had a mindset.

Where did it come from? “With all them whose spirit God had raised.” You brothers and sisters in this fight, God put that spirit on you to join. It is not of your own doing; each of you was called into this truth.

“To go up to build the house of the Lord”: that is the key part. You were not called to sit; you were called to build. Building has many elements: permits, electric, foundation, roof, drywall, paint. How is it you can't find anything to do? You can't stack papers? There has got to be something you can do in this great, vast work.

“But without thy mind would I do nothing.” You have to have the mindset of a leader to get anything done. You have to see it mentally and visualize it before it happens. That is how important the mindset of a leader is, “that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly.”

precepts.why:
“So built we the wall.” All through our history our forefathers were building, and what we do now is no different. As the Bishop brings out about the little sanctuaries, what we do today is no different from what our forefathers always did. Paul went to Galatia, Colossae, Corinth and Thessalonica: those were sanctuaries, just like the ones you see today, and each of us has put a hand into building every one of them.

“For the people had a mind to work.” You have to have a mindset to get the work done. Some people talk about what we can't do: who told you that, the white man? Our forefathers got done every task that came up against them. The Maccabees defeated their enemies; our fathers were slaves in Egypt, and Egypt was the America of today, the same situation we are in. If the white man starts shooting at us, we know scripturally what is going to happen. We are not violent, but Christ is; the Lord is going to take care of it.

sense.text: This is how a leader's mindset must be when you have that mind to work. “The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.” You have to be locked in, laser focused. Whatever you are locked in on is all you will see and all that matters. And when the leader is like that, everybody underneath him will be like that too.
“A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered.”

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers.” However the leader is, that is how the men under him will be. When you see other camps that look disorganized, talking about rape, that have not built anything in years, find their leaders and you will see why. When you see us traveling all over the world building institutions, look at our leaders: we are the representation of our leadership. A bishop or deacon will never put out a video eating chicken and pizza in the hood at midnight; when we went to O'Block in Chicago, we were teaching the word of the Lord.

Everything rises and falls on leadership. In some cities the leader is changed out and the camp takes off. That is why everyone wants to ask the Bishop for the secret sauce, but Christ is at the head and we all follow Christ. The Most High is building 144,000 leaders sealed with the law of God, and with all their VR glasses, AI and OnlyFans they cannot stop it.

A leader believes and does everything for the people around him. Leadership is not just telling everybody what to do; a true leader guides and does all his actions for those around him, because being a leader is being a servant.

“For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he.” The thoughts that come into your mind, what you see and visualize, are what will be manifested. You are the evidence of your thoughts, and nobody is anywhere by surprise unless he is in denial. Women may be surprised where they are because they do not believe in accountability, but the men should know where they are and why. If you have a pot belly, you have not been eating right. If you are not making the money or living in the neighborhood you want, it is your fault: you have poor thoughts, or your thoughts are not matched by your actions. Think about a double cheeseburger from Five Guys day and night and you will end up there. If you keep asking why you can't get a better job, you are not putting forth the actions to make it happen.

A true leader serves the people around him, and the higher you go, the more people you serve. Deacon Yasha is over many offices and gets so many requests that you have to email him or his phone will blow up. A captain of 200 has to serve 200 people; an officer of 80 serves 80 men, their wives, and their four or five children each.

So be mindful of what you ask for. Some brothers work underhandedly to become leaders, asking for the 50's test. This is the Lord's business and he gives it out; the brothers who always ask never make it, and that is how you know Satan is pushing them. Nine times out of ten the brother who asks for the test fails it, because spiritually he is not ready. Nobody asks to be a leader; the Lord raised these men up. The Bishop did not ask to be a bishop.

“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” Go after the flattering title and your maker will soon take you away: you get the test and fail. When the student is ready the teacher will be there; promotion comes from the Lord, and once you fulfill your office he will make it happen. Many brothers who wanted position fell down into the abyss and never made it back, while the brothers who were down come back on fire. The work will determine where you are supposed to be. Some get jealous when a brother is put over them; just do the work of the Lord. If you love the Lord you will work for the Lord and not for position. In Maccabees the brother who wanted to get himself a name ended up put to death.

“Let us shew an example to our brethren.” That is the question to ask yourself: you want to be a leader, but is your house in order? What are your works, to be an example to others? This truth is about being an example. Christ is the ultimate example; he is the most famous man on the face of the earth because of his works, the one man who did nothing wrong and was put to death for it.

“Because their hearts depend upon us”: the nation depends on its leaders. That is why America went straight after the leaders, because that is where your hope and faith come from, and why they took out Martin and Malcolm when they were getting too big. This movement is different because all of us have the same guideline and the same instructions; everybody runs the same playbook over and over, and it keeps working. The commandments are the secret sauce.

“And the sanctuary, and the house, and the altar, rest upon us.” Your position is to be an example, not only here but at your house, at your job, with your wife, with your children, in what you eat and how you treat your temple. Are you ready to be examined like that? All of that is part of being a leader.

Here is a great leader whose mind was on the people, because that is what leadership is: caring for those around you. “Thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people”: “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad.” Solomon had the opportunity to lead, and he asked for wisdom to deal with all those people. He understood the mission. He did not ask for 400 women and chariots on 20s, and he did not ask to be tested for the king of 4,000.

“And the speech pleased the Lord”, because Solomon had “not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment.”

“Lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee.” His mindset was on the people, and because he had a mind for the people the Lord elevated him and gave him more than he desired for himself. Likewise with us: when we have a mind for the people and it is not for ourselves, the Lord will bless it beyond measure.

“Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” In this truth we are not doing it for ourselves. Captains left at four in the morning to be here to help teach; Captain Shamaya drove down and arrived at five to check the congregation and the saints of the Most High. The Bishops and Deacons travel all over the world. It is for the nation of Israel, because we understand the kingdom at hand.

You must be nation-minded. Too often it is me, me, me. All through the Bible the greatest leaders were focused on the nation of Israel and on how to move the nation further ahead.
“The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life.” “The good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.”

“But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd”, when he “seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth.” You find out who your leaders are when tribulation comes: when things get hard, some run, and others stand ten toes and figure out how to get the job done. Brothers have picked up and moved their whole families: Captain Sham to New Orleans, Deacon Yashar to Phoenix, Captain Zakar to Sacramento, brothers to Tijuana, and soon brothers will move to the other side of the earth. That is what a true shepherd does. The hireling “careth not for the sheep.”

“I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep”: “and I lay down my life for the sheep.” That is the mindset we must have. The brothers at the forefront of this movement understand the target on their backs. They already know who we are. Nobody knew who the Ayatollah was until last week, but the men leading marches all over the world, 300 boots on the ground in Madagascar, 2,000 men on the streets of a capital, establishments in Africa: they know who we are. Know what you are part of, so that when it is your time you are not shaking and trembling.
“We returned all of us to the wall, every one unto his work.”

“The half of my servants wrought in the work, and the other half of them held both the spears, the shields, and the bows.” While they worked, they had to be ready to fight at the same time. That is what we are doing. Many of us are part-time prophets: nine hours a day at work, and the second you get off, it is the camp and the flyer mission. When the boss asks if that was you out there, it was my nephew; I know not the man.

“Every one with one of his hands wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon.” We are fighting two battles at the same time, and some brothers fight three, because there is a dragon at home too.

A true leader transfers his belief onto others. “Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow.” A true leader imparts his faith to the next man. Think of the level of faith the Bishop had to have for this truth to be where it is in IUIC. The impact of the Bishop and Deacons reaches well beyond the purple and gold: people outside IUIC donate to the booster club; they may not join or fully understand, but they respect it, and the little camps teaching at noon or three all tune in at six on Saturday night.

“Considering the end of their conversation.” Good leaders make you believe in them; great leaders make you believe in yourself. That is how the Bishop raises up other bishops, deacons, captains, and soldiers by the thousands.

precepts.why: “Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Then: “That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” How do you think that made Peter feel, Christ telling him he would build his church upon him? That is what great leaders do: they empower and strengthen others and make you believe in yourself, not in them.

Moses prayed, “let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan”, but the Lord said, “Let it suffice thee”, and showed him the land from the top of Pisgah: “thou shalt not go over this Jordan.”

“But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land.” That is your job as a leader: to encourage and strengthen the men around you.
“Behold, thou hast instructed many”: your job as a leader is to instruct many. “And thou hast strengthened the weak hands”: it is your job to build up the brothers and the sisters in the spirit.

“But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you are converted, strengthen your brothers. Peter answered that he was ready to go with him to prison and to death, and Christ told him that he would thrice deny that he knew him.

Paul “went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.” Strengthening all the disciples in these various countries is the job of a leader. As the Bishops and Deacons blazed the trail, the captains follow the same path: in Guyana and South America our brothers and sisters are growing tremendously.

“Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me.” That is our job: we must strengthen one another. You get weak at different times; you need counsel, exhortation, sometimes to vent, and a leader must be there to strengthen.

When you first come into the truth you just edit the video, go to the flyer mission or work in the kitchen. At some point you are over the office, over the brothers editing, the IT team, the building team, the sisters, and your job changes. Not everybody is built for that level, but it can be learned. You are not in charge; you are responsible for those in your charge. You must guide those people, not just tell everybody what to do.

sense.text: In rebuilding Jerusalem, men started off building a section: “Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah”.

“And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem.” Now he was a supervisor over that area. In IUIC there are different offices with leads in place: there was once one main man responsible for an office, and then the Lord entrusted him with more.

Brothers sometimes get overwhelmed with their office, and that will happen. But there is nothing better to be overwhelmed for than the Lord. You do not have a demon on your back, you are not behind bars or suffering illness; you are stressed for the Lord's work, and that is a beautiful thing. Rather than complain, come and ask for more assistance, pray and fast for more laborers, and rejoice, because the Lord gave you that office.
The last part: a leader leads by example. “Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.”

“Shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.” A true leader shows you his faith by his works. As the Bishop said years ago, if your Israelite leader is not about building institutions all over the world, you are following the wrong person, because we understand where this truth is going and what is about to happen in the end times. Make not thyself an underling to a foolish man: if your leader is not about prepping for what is coming, not about prophecy, marriage, order and discipline, you are in the wrong place.

Our forefathers are the examples: David led by example when he killed Goliath, and Paul led by example through the persecutions he went through.

precepts.why:
“He that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.” “I am among you as he that serveth.” If Christ is serving, what do you have to be on your high horse about?

In Sierra Leone, the second poorest country in the world, with no hot water, no fast food and no movies, a week and a half felt long. The Bishop did a month out there by himself because the Lord told him to, doing two or three radio shows a day until he lost his voice. Those early recordings of his voice were from Sierra Leone. He is a servant; you have to really love the Lord and be locked in.

The Bishop, the Deacons, all of us take that sacrifice, because the sacrifice cannot compare to what the people gain from it. In Guyana there was no hot water either, but the souls were built up, and we are doing that worldwide because all of our people are in a decayed state.

sense.text:
We are the leaders of today, each and every one of us. “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places”: there is that word build again. “Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations”: how? Through marriage. It is no coincidence that IUIC is the one camp that focuses on marriage.

“And thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in.” We shall be known as the restorer of paths to dwell in: twelve tribes, worldwide.
